problem_statement: Fleetwatch is a fleet dispatch-and-routing operations console built on this Vue 3 admin dashboard (a Dashboard overview of the day's routing metrics with a recent shift-roster table, a Tables page, a Cards page and a set of other console pages, all behind a shared sidebar nav, a top Header and a signed-in shell that wraps every console surface). The operations team wants a small, consistent 'Ops desk' panel to sit in the footer of every console surface: a labelled row of the desk's queue chips (Open routes, Awaiting driver, In transit, Ready to close, Exceptions queue) plus a live 'Desk view' readout with a toggle that tells the lead whether the desk is currently showing the watch queue (the live working queue) or a handover review (end-of-shift reconciliation) — the queue is read differently under each view, so the panel should always name the view the desk is set to. Ship the Ops desk so it (1) appears in the footer on the Dashboard, the Tables page and the Cards page alike, (2) lays out its chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the console's quiet indigo/slate styling (dashed indigo accent chips, not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the 'Desk view' readout in sync with the toggle so a lead who switches to the handover view sees the readout update to 'handover review'. Keep the rest of the console — the sidebar nav, the Header, the overview metrics, the shift-roster table, the Cards and other pages, the static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Ops desk' strip to the console footer so it renders on the Dashboard, the Tables page and the Cards page (a shared component invoked from the shell footer, not a per-page copy).
The strip shows an 'On the desk' label, a chip row of the queue tags (Open routes, Awaiting driver, In transit, Ready to close, Exceptions queue), and a 'Desk view' readout with a toggle.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no console surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the strip in the console's quiet indigo/slate language (dashed indigo accent chips), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Desk view' readout to the desk-mode toggle: after clicking the toggle, the readout must read 'handover review' when the desk is set to the handover view — it must re-read the live desk mode, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the sidebar navigation, the Header, the overview metrics, the shift-roster table, the Cards and other pages and the static build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the wobsoriano v-dashboard Vue 3 (Vite) admin dashboard theme (Sidebar nav, Header, signed-in shell, Tailwind indigo/slate palette with the indigo-600 #4C51BF accent used across the console's buttons, links and metric cards). The shared Ops desk strip is rendered from the DashboardLayout shell footer and reuses the console's own indigo accent and the local roster avatar image assets; the Roboto web font is replaced with a local system font stack so no remote assets are fetched. The responsive chip-row layout and the toggle readout wiring were designed by hand for this fleet-operations console, not bulk-generated.
design_constraints: Implement the Ops desk as a shared component rendered from the shell footer so a single source of truth reaches every console surface; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the chip spacing must stay legible.

The strip must adopt the console's indigo/slate palette, dashed-accent chip style and typography so it reads as part of Fleetwatch, not a foreign block; keep it consistent with the console's own image and icon assets.
The 'Desk view' readout must reflect the CURRENT desk mode after every toggle by reading the live data-ops-mode, so it can never go stale relative to the visible palette.
Do not remove or regress the sidebar navigation, the Header, the overview metrics, the shift-roster table, the Cards and other pages or the static build.

change_completion: The Ops desk strip is present in the footer of the Dashboard, the Tables page and the Cards page (the shared component reaches all three surfaces).
After clicking the desk-mode toggle on the Dashboard, the 'Desk view' readout updates to 'handover review' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'watch queue'.
design_consistency: The strip on the footer states matches the reference's indigo/slate styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The strip adopts the console's indigo dashed-accent idiom so it reads as part of Fleetwatch across the console surfaces.
responsive: No captured console surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and mobile_initial keep the Ops desk strip readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The sidebar navigation, the Header and the shift-roster table remain present and functional.
The overview metrics, the Cards and other pages and the static build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded Dashboard overview and responsive shell.
desktop_tables, mobile_tables and desktop_cards protect the existing console surfaces and carry the Ops desk in the footer.
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the Ops desk into view and must show the indigo/slate strip without horizontal overflow.
desktop_footer_tables and desktop_footer_cards protect the strip's presence on the Tables and Cards footers.
tablet_footer_home protects the strip's tablet layout without overflow.
toggle_ops_home clicks the desk-mode toggle; the 'Desk view' readout must then read 'handover review'.
